launch_default_media_receiver.description: LAUNCH the Default Media Receiver (appId CC1AD845) on the receiver namespace.

load_media.description: LOAD a media URL into the running receiver session (media namespace). contentId is the URL; contentType is its MIME type.

mime.description: MIME type, e.g. video/mp4 or audio/mpeg.

url.description: Media URL for the receiver to fetch (e.g. a self-hosted MP4/MP3).

stop_app.description: STOP the running receiver app (receiver namespace).

txt_match.description: The device UUID; its presence marks a Cast device.

methods.notes: Cast devices advertise _googlecast._tcp with TXT records fn (friendly name), md (model), id (UUID) and ca. The UUID is the stable identity; fn is the display name.

mdns_txt_match.description: Cast devices publish a stable UUID in the mDNS TXT 'id' record.

device.name: Google Chromecast (CASTv2)
device.notes:
Chromecast is Google's media-receiver line — the original Chromecast dongles, Chromecast Audio, and Chromecast with Google TV — plus the CASTv2 receiver baked into many third-party TVs and speakers. Google ended Chromecast hardware production in August 2024 (replaced by the Google TV Streamer) and gave the 4K/HD models security updates only into September 2025, so the dongles themselves are now an abandoned line. The CASTv2 protocol lives on in Cast-enabled devices.
Local relevance: discovery + CASTv2 control + the Default Media Receiver can load and control arbitrary media URLs entirely on the LAN, with no Google account touched at control time. (Most streaming APPS still require their own cloud; this spec scopes to local casting of self-hosted media and basic receiver control, not the app ecosystem.)
TRANSPORT: a TLS socket to TCP 8009 carrying length-prefixed protobuf CastMessages. Framing is a 32-bit big-endian length prefix followed by a CastMessage (protocol_version, source_id, destination_id, namespace, payload_type STRING|BINARY, payload_utf8/payload_binary). Platform endpoints are sender-0 / receiver-0; session endpoints use dynamic ids like client-<n>.
NAMESPACES:
  urn:x-cast:com.google.cast.tp.connection  — virtual connection CONNECT/CLOSE
  urn:x-cast:com.google.cast.tp.heartbeat   — PING/PONG (sender PINGs ~every 5s;
                                               no PONG => connection dead)
  urn:x-cast:com.google.cast.receiver       — LAUNCH / STOP / GET_STATUS apps
  urn:x-cast:com.google.cast.tp.deviceauth  — device authentication handshake
  urn:x-cast:com.google.cast.media          — LOAD / PLAY / PAUSE / SEEK / STOP

APP IDs (LAUNCH via the receiver namespace): Default Media Receiver CC1AD845, Backdrop E8C28D3C, YouTube 233637DE, DashCast 84912283, BubbleUPnP 3927FA74. With the Default Media Receiver a client LOADs a contentId + contentType and then PLAY/PAUSE/SEEK it — the local-media path.

openness.notes: Google publishes sender SDKs but not the wire protocol; CASTv2 was reverse-engineered by the community. node-castv2 is the canonical description; pychromecast (Home Assistant) is the reference Python client.

credentials.notes: CASTv2 control on the LAN is not user-authenticated (a device-auth handshake exists on the deviceauth namespace but does not gate local media control). The Wi-Fi passphrase is handled by the Home app's provisioning, not by anything this spec documents.

factory_reset.effect: Clears Wi-Fi credentials and the device's Home/account binding, returning it to setup. Performed by holding the button on the device (or from the Home app); the exact hold time is model-specific.

procedures.basis: Google documents a button-hold reset per model; not replayed here.
procedures.name: Button-hold factory reset

steps.action: Hold the device's physical button until the LED indicates a reset, then release.
steps.expect: The device reboots into setup mode.

cloud.local_alternative: Yes for CONTROL — discovery (mDNS) and CASTv2 (TLS 8009) drive the device locally once it is on the network. Initial Wi-Fi provisioning, however, requires the Google Home app and a Google account; there is no documented account-free provisioning path.

methods.description: Factory setup joins the device to Wi-Fi via the Google Home app (Google account required for setup). After that, local CASTv2 control and Default-Media-Receiver playback work on the LAN with no account.

steps.action: Provision the device onto Wi-Fi with the Google Home app (Google account).
Discover it via _googlecast._tcp and open a TLS connection to port 8009 for local control.

setup.notes: Initial Wi-Fi onboarding runs through the Google Home app and a Google account; the onboarding wire protocol is not documented here. Once on the LAN, discovery and CASTv2 control need no account.

rejoin.notes: Changing Wi-Fi networks is done through the Google Home app; there is no documented local-protocol path to re-provision credentials, so a network change is effectively a reprovision.

testing.notes: Not driven against hardware by this project. The transport (TLS 8009, length-prefixed protobuf), namespaces, heartbeat and mDNS string are from node-castv2 and pychromecast; app IDs from pychromecast's config.

castv2_protocol.framing: 32-bit big-endian length prefix, then a protobuf CastMessage with fields protocol_version, source_id, destination_id, namespace, payload_type (STRING|BINARY) and payload_utf8/payload_binary.
castv2_protocol.heartbeat: Sender PINGs on the heartbeat namespace ~every 5s; a missing PONG means the link is dead.
